thread:
maria: heads-up: we just got a Severity 2 from AcmeCorp — they say p95 and p99 generation latency jumped ~3x for some endpoints around 03:18 UTC. support-bot created INC-5012. putting it here since dashboards disagree on whether it's a real client-side regression or a rollup artifact.

kevin: pulling it up now. which dashboard are they looking at? the public customer dashboard or internal per-model latency?

maria: customer-facing dashboard (platform/redwood-api/models/latency) shows p95 ~240ms -> 750ms at 03:18. internal per-host histograms (traces) show median drift but p95 only moved to ~300ms. so weird disparity.

sre-bot: alert: latency_p95_high (rule: p95_over_500ms) fired for route=/v1/generate (severity=warning) at 2026-03-15T03:20:05Z.

kevin: ok can you paste the dashboard query and the raw histogram query? I'm worried about rollup/aggregation vs raw series.

maria: dashboard metric (Grafana panel):
```
max_over_time(quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) ), 5m)
```
Raw histogram query from traces:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))
```
Dashboard uses a `quantile_over_time` on pre-aggregated rollups, traces use fresh per-host rollup.

alex: that first query screams "double aggregation" to me — quantile_over_time on already-rolled-up bucket counts can produce inflated quantiles if bucket boundaries are rebinned or if some hosts have sparse sampling. any recent changes to metrics pipeline or rollup rules?

maria: ops-bot deployed a metrics rebin job at 03:15 as part of the telemetry housekeeping run.

ops-bot: deployment: telemetry/rebin-job v2.3 was rolled out to staging at 03:10 and production at 03:15 by @ops. Link: https://ci.internal/deploy/telemetry/rebin-job/2.3

linda: that aligns perfectly. rebinning changed bucket boundaries from: `[0.001,0.005,0.01,0.025,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2,5]` to `[0.002,0.008,0.02,0.04,0.08,0.2,0.4,0.8,1.6,3.2]` (example). when you rebin existing rollups you can get weird step changes in computed quantiles because aggregation assumes consistent buckets.

kevin: can you show quick repro with a simple synthetic example to illustrate how quantiles diverge after rebin?

linda: sure. small example: per-host durations (ms): hostA: [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] hostB: [10, 15, 20, 25, 30]. true combined p95 ~47ms. compute per-host p95 then take max -> ~50ms. Now if rebin maps some values into coarser buckets and rollup sums buckets before computing quantile_over_time, the algorithm approximates and can jump to ~70ms. TL;DR: percentiles of aggregates != aggregates of percentiles.

maria: thanks. so immediate ask: what quick mitigation can we do for customers? revert rebin job? change dashboards to use raw_series?

alex: short term: flip the customer dashboard to read from `raw_series` (non-rollup) for the last 24h and show both `histogram_quantile` over sum(rate(...)) and the existing panel so support can see both. medium term: roll back rebin job and re-run with a migration that preserves old boundaries for 48h.

kevin: agree. also add a note to billing/support template that this is visualization artifact unless traces/backing hist still show real regressions. don't touch model rollout yet.

support-bot: INC-5012 update: Notified AcmeCorp that we're investigating. ETA for next update: 03:50 UTC.

maria: I'll make the dashboard change now (read-only clone + toggle). pushing a patch to grafana: `grafana/dashboards/latency-panel` branch `fix/rollup-source` with a flag to select `raw_series`.

ops-bot: deployment triggered: grafana/dashboards/latency-panel (patch) by maria at 03:27.

kevin: while we do that, let's confirm whether any real client-side request latencies increased. run a quick sampled trace compare for route=/v1/generate between 03:00-03:14 and 03:18-03:30 across 10k requests.

maria: running: `curl -s https://internal-api/metrics/query -d 'q=histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))' &> p95_pre.txt` and same for the post window. results: pre p95 ~230ms, post p95 ~260ms (per-host aggregated). Not 750ms.

alex: good — suggests visualization artifact. but we need to confirm no customer errors. check error rate, 5xx, and retries.

maria: error rate normal. Retries spiked slightly for one Dedicated pool due to a transient gRPC connect timeout around 03:12 but that is unrelated; resolved by autoscaler bounce at 03:16.

linda: action items: 1) short-term: switch customer dashboard to raw_series + annotation indicating rollup change (owner: maria, ETA 03:45). 2) mid-term: roll back rebin job OR run a migration that preserves historical buckets (owner: ops, ETA 6h). 3) longer-term: update telemetry to versioned bucket metadata so dashboards can automatically detect rollup boundary changes and annotate (owner: alex, ETA 2 weeks). 4) update support template to explain visualization vs real regressions (owner: kevin, ETA 1h).

kevin: I'll draft the support message. also add a runbook step: `if p95 discrepancy > 2x between customer-dashboard and per-host-histogram, check recent telemetry deployments and rebin jobs` and link to this thread.

sre-bot: incident status: INC-5012 set to investigating. priority: P2. subscribed: maria, kevin, alex, linda, ops.

maria: dashboard clone pushed, switched to raw_series, and added annotation about telemetry/rebin at 03:26 UTC. support updated AcmeCorp with preliminary note that this looks like a metrics artifact, not a model regression.

support-bot: INC-5012 update: customer acknowledged, wants final confirmation after rollback/migration.

alex: ops — please confirm whether rollback is safe. if rollback touches a large historical dataset it could be expensive. maybe better to create a compatibility layer that presents both boundary sets to the dashboard (cheap), then plan migration.

ops-bot: acknowledged. starting a quick risk assessment for rollback vs compatibility shim. ETA 4h.

kevin: good job triaging quickly. once we finalize, let's summarize in postmortem-style note even though this was a false-positive so we can avoid panic next time. include the exact queries and a minimal reproducible example (Linda's numbers) so support can explain it succinctly.

maria: agreed. I'll record the snippet and attach it to the INC.

linda: one more technical note for the runbook: when using quantile approximation over rollups, set the `max_error` param lower (e.g., 0.01) during critical windows to reduce step artifacts. also prefer `histogram_quantile` on summed counts for accuracy.

kevin: thanks everyone. leaving this thread as the canonical link. assign follow-ups in INC-5012. closing communications loop for now. :white_check_mark:
